kitPage.title: Seiðr-kit — showcase
kitPage.lead: Every shared LORE v2 element on one page, as it looks in the dark amber Seiðr theme, on colour tokens and the --fs-2xs…--fs-2xl scale.
kitPage.pal.lead: Ctrl+K — records and commands, “/” — search records; with no query — recent items. Keys work in any keyboard layout.
kitPage.sh.sheetBody: Side panel: focus is trapped inside, Esc closes it.
kitPage.md.sample:
## Decision

admin.title: Admin
admin.agents.title: Agents
admin.agents.lead: Which harness each agent runs in, on which machine and whose it is. “Not set” and “not linked” mean no data, not “as intended”.
admin.agents.truncated: Not all agents shown: the server truncated the result.
admin.rules.title: CLAUDE rules
admin.rules.lead: CLAUDE rules docs (kind claude-rules): body and versions. The comparison view depends on what the server returns.
admin.rules.fileNote: The rules file lives on the machine — neither the browser nor the server can see it. The doc-vs-file diff is computed by MCP claude_rules_diff; sync is claude_rules_push and claude_rules_pull.
admin.rules.pickHint: Pick a rules doc to see its body and versions.
admin.rules.unknownDoc: Doc {id} is not among CLAUDE rules.
admin.rules.htmlOnly: The doc has only an HTML body — MD bodies are shown here.
admin.rules.outsideScope: Versions exist but are outside your projects — this is not "no history".
admin.rules.noVersions: The doc has no SCD2 versions: writing a doc does not create versions — nothing to compare.
admin.rules.oneVersion: The doc has one version — nothing to compare with.
admin.rules.pickVersion: Which version to compare with the previous one
admin.rules.coarse: The texts are long — the diff is coarse: everything removed and everything added as a whole.
admin.rules.noBodies: The server does not return version bodies — no line diff; body changes are visible by hash.
admin.col.author: Author
admin.flags.title: Flags and version
admin.flags.lead: Which build LORE runs and which lore.* flags differ from their defaults.
admin.flags.releaseNone: the deploy did not pass a release tag
admin.flags.noneChanged: All flags are at their defaults.
admin.harness.dictEmpty: The harness dictionary is empty — the migration has not run yet. Editing is unavailable, shown as is.
admin.harness.dictError: Could not read the harness dictionary ({reason}) — editing is unavailable, shown as is.
admin.who.title: Who is where
admin.who.lead: How many projects each person is in, their role in each and their agents. An agent sees all of its owner’s projects, so a project runs the agents of all its members.
admin.who.agentsError: Agents could not be read ({reason}) — people and roles shown, agents not.
admin.who.orphans: Agents without an owner among people ({n}):
admin.log.title: Action journal
admin.log.lead: Who changed what in LORE: when, in which family, over which record, human or agent, and how it ended. Refusals are as visible as successes.
admin.log.emptyHint: No mutating calls in admin families yet: a verified zero, not a failed read.
admin.log.emptyFilterHint: The journal is not empty — no record just fits these conditions. Clear the filter to see the whole journal.
admin.log.forbiddenHint: Only an administrator sees the action journal. This is not an empty journal — it was not given to you.
admin.log.badParamsAllowed: The server listed the allowed values:
admin.log.totalExact: Showing {shown} of {total} records under the filter.
admin.log.totalUnknown: Records shown: {shown}. How many there are in total under the filter is unknown: the server could not count. That is neither zero nor «all of them».
admin.log.truncated: Output cut by the limit of {limit}: there are more records than shown. Raise the limit or narrow the period.
admin.log.truncatedNoLimit: Output was cut: there are more records than shown, and the server did not name the limit. Narrow the period.
admin.log.f.timeHint: Period: a date (2026-11-10), an ISO instant (2026-11-10T12:00:00Z) or epoch millis. A date in «To» takes the whole day.
admin.log.batch.nothing: There is nothing to expand: no role events carry this batch id. This is not «the batch was empty» — that is how batches applied before this rollout, dry runs and no-op batches look.
admin.log.batch.error: The batch did not expand ({reason}) — a failed read, not «no such batch». You can retry.
admin.log.batch.undoOpen: The undo window is still open — until {until}.
admin.log.batch.undoClosed: The undo window is closed (it was open until {until}): the server will refuse an undo.
admin.log.batch.undoUnknown: The server did not name the undo deadline — we treat the window as closed until it says otherwise.
admin.log.batch.rollbackHint: We first show what will change and ask for the person's id — as in “Roles”.
admin.log.batch.rollbackClosed: This batch cannot be rolled back from here: the undo window is closed or its deadline is unknown.
admin.log.batch.rollbackNoBody: This batch cannot be rolled back from here: the server sent no rollback body.
admin.machine.title: Machine
admin.machine.noOwner: No editing: the agent has no owner, and the server links a machine only together with one.
admin.machine.noClient: No editing: the agent has no account (client_id), and the server will not accept the request without it.
admin.machine.hint: A miniLORE machine (client_id minilore-link-*) is one per name; lore-mcp-* agents on one machine share the name legitimately.
admin.roles.sources.hint: Keycloak — the person's realm roles; Forgejo is not asked yet: there is no link between the LORE user and a Forgejo user. Read-only.
admin.mcp.title: MCP
admin.mcp.lead: MCP connections and failures by agent profile — what LORE sees from calls. A profile silent for long is marked “not seen”, not “healthy”.
admin.mcp.profilesNote: These are profiles (full, pm, …), not sessions: LORE cannot tell sessions of one Keycloak client apart.
admin.mcp.emptyHint: This is not “all fine”: LORE simply has not seen a single MCP call.
admin.mcp.failError: Could not read failures ({reason}) — connections are shown, nothing is claimed about failures.
admin.mcp.truncated: Not all profiles shown: the server truncated the result.
admin.mcp.health.stale: not seen for over a day
kitPage.flow.lead: Wizard steps: order, a named reason when you cannot go on, going back without losing input, the step in the URL, and a final “left to do by hand” list.
kitPage.flow.s3lead: A real screen would preview the changes here.
kitPage.flow.manual1: Hand over the password in person
kitPage.flow.doneSaid: Wizard finished — the app would now perform the action.
kitPage.flow.diffUnver: This row could not be verified
kitPage.flow.diffApplied: The app received {n} row(s) — it then applies them as one batch with an undo window.
kitPage.flow.batchHead: The batch: undo window and partial failure
kitPage.flow.matrixHead: The matrix: a value in the cell and the check state
kitPage.flow.matrixLead: The matrix applies nothing: proposals go to the diff, and the diff to the batch with an undo window.
kitPage.flow.matrixProposed: Changes proposed: {n} — the diff shows them next.
kitPage.flow.chainHead: Why this verdict: the outcome and its chain of reasons
kitPage.flow.chainLead: The outcome in one line, and under it the steps in the order they decided. A step has five outcomes, not two: confirmed · ruled out · could not verify · not allowed to look · not asked. The decisive step is marked, and a chain cut short says so.
kitPage.flow.chainUnaskedWhy: the source is switched off in the settings
kitPage.flow.chainStopWhy: the rest was not computed — the outcome was already settled
kitPage.flow.relHead: Content release: version diff and activation
kitPage.flow.relLead: The release class (hotfix or release) is computed by the server — the showcase shows what was sent. Activation and rollback go through a confirmation.
admin.who.mineUnknown: All mine: could not check your projects
admin.access.title: Effective access
admin.access.realmHint: The realm role is known to Keycloak, not the graph — take it from the KC card (viewer, editor, admin…). Empty — no realm role.
admin.access.pickHint: Pick a project — the server explains whether this person sees it and why.
admin.access.scopeOff: Project scope is off on the server — every signed-in user sees the project now.
admin.access.nobody: Nobody has a role in the project — only bypassing realm roles see it.
admin.access.bypass: Realm roles that bypass the scope:
admin.access.agentsSeeForbidden: Agent scope not shown: no permission.
admin.access.noAgentsSee: No agents — no projects are inherited.
admin.access.agentsSeeYour: Your agents ({a}) see your {n} projects — inherited from you.
admin.access.agentsSeeHis: Their agents ({a}) see their {n} projects — inherited from the owner.
admin.access.noClient: The agent has no client_id — project inheritance cannot be checked.
admin.access.ownerNoProjects: The owner has no project roles — nothing for the agent to inherit.
admin.access.noScope: Agent profile is not set — where it writes cannot be checked; read access only.
admin.roles.title: Roles
admin.roles.lead: A person's roles across all their projects: groups by role, search, multi-select and a matrix. Every change goes through a diff, typing the login and a batch with undo.
admin.roles.forbidden: No permission to view people's roles
admin.roles.forbiddenHint: Only a LORE administrator (admin role) can see and change people's roles.
admin.roles.empty: No people in the graph yet
admin.roles.emptyHint: A person appears here once they are granted their first project role.
admin.roles.pick: Pick a person to open their roles card.
admin.roles.notFound: Person {id} is not in the role matrix — the link is stale or they have no roles any more.
admin.roles.rowUnverified: the server did not confirm the roles were read in full
admin.roles.none: The person has no project roles (checked in the graph).
admin.roles.noMatch: No project matches the search — roles exist, just not under this word.
admin.roles.panelHint: Nothing is applied right away: first a diff for all selected projects and one confirmation by login.
admin.roles.matrixHint: Clicking a cell or “set the whole row” is a proposal: the diff with confirmation applies it.
admin.roles.danger.title: What changes for {name}
admin.roles.danger.loading: The server is computing the diff…
admin.roles.danger.need: Until the login is typed exactly, nothing can be applied.
admin.roles.danger.logged: The batch is recorded in the action journal.
kitPage.chips.title: Chip values
kitPage.chips.lead: A field value may arrive as an object: an id for the link, a label for the human, and a mark of inheritance. The row shows the first three, the rest sit under “N more”. An inherited chip says where it came from — “the task’s project” and “its sprint’s project” are different claims. No label means the id is shown, not emptiness.
